category_title: Students who actively distance themselves from non-reading family environments
minimal_context: The student is participating in 30 minutes of independent reading using the assigned whole-class text.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Demetrius, it is time for our 30 minutes of independent reading. Please take out the assigned class novel and begin reading the next chapter.

STUDENT: Okay, I have it out. I will try to read it.

TUTOR: Just focus on the pages we need to cover today.

STUDENT: I'm trying, but it's hard for me to read this specific book. We are not really a family that reads that much, except for me, so I'm used to just reading by myself when I find something I like.

TUTOR: Keep trying, we all have to read this same book for the course.

STUDENT: I know that if you read you do better in school or English, and I really want to get a good grade. But I wasn't really raised to be read to, and I just can't get through this assigned text no matter how politely I sit here.

options.A: Incorporate frequent opportunities for the student to respond (OTRs) during whole-class instruction and the independent reading period.
options.B: Provide clear color-coded signs (green for talk, red for quiet) to indicate talk and no-talk times or quiet work zones during independent reading.
options.C: Provide written feedback using a 3-point Likert-type scale ranging from 1 (needs improvement) to 3 (great job) after independent reading.
options.D: Emphasize student self-selection of all reading texts and an individualized approach to assessment during the independent reading period and course.
